_meta.name: spacecraft_zone_type_modifiers
_meta.description: Zone-type modifiers for closed-loop spacecraft environments (ISS-analog, starship). Applied on top of iss_baseline_profile.json. Unlike maritime modifiers, there is no marine environmental input. All zones are fully enclosed with HEPA-filtered recirculated air. Microbial variation between zones is driven primarily by human activity patterns and equipment.

units.taxon_multipliers: dimensionless multiplicative factors; neutral value is 1.0
units.marker_additions: small relative-abundance priors before final renormalization

Dining.description: Shared dining/galley area: oral and skin carryover from crew, food preparation residue, elevated Streptococcus and Lactobacillus from oral microbiome.

Room.description: Crew quarters / berthing: dominated by skin commensals (Staphylococcus, Corynebacterium, Malassezia). Highest Staphylococcus abundance of any zone type. Closed sleeping environment concentrates shed skin cells.

Free.description: General-purpose areas (bridge/command, labs, corridors, recreation). Mixed microbial sources. Closest to the baseline ISS profile. Moderate diversity from varied human activity.

Engine_Room.description: Engineering / life support / environmental control. Elevated extremophile-tolerant organisms from equipment surfaces. Higher Methylobacterium, Ralstonia (water system associated), and Burkholderia. No thermophilic archaea (unlike maritime engine rooms) — spacecraft engineering sections are temperature-controlled.

Medical.description: Sickbay / medical bay. Elevated antimicrobial-resistant organisms. Higher Enterobacter and Klebsiella from clinical specimens. Lower fungal diversity due to antifungal protocols. Elevated opportunistic pathogens.
